title: Khufu (Cheops)
summary: Khufu, called Cheops by the Greeks, was the second king of Egypt's 4th Dynasty and the builder of the Great Pyramid at Giza. Egypt's antiquities ministry dates his reign to about 2589–2566 BCE, though its length is debated. Papyri from Wadi al-Jarf date from near its end.

uncertainty.note: Reign dates differ by source (c. 2589–2566 BC; 2590–2568 BC; c. 2585–2560 BCE). Length is disputed: the Turin canon gives 23 years, but Tallet reads a logbook dated to Year 26.

as_recorded.value: reign circa 2585-2560 b.c.e. in one entry; the Turin Canon lists twenty-three years
year after the 13th census of Cheops (Year 26), the last known year of this king's reign

where.historical_name: Memphite royal necropolis at Giza, Old Kingdom Egypt (4th Dynasty)

importance.justification: Builder of the Great Pyramid, the best-known monument of the Old Kingdom.

related.because: He commissioned the Great Pyramid as his tomb.
